content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps enumerated forward: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (new alkene). 3) Sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic steps: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment (the part /C=C/C(=O)N...) came from aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid. So we need to disconnect the C=C double bond and the carboxylic acid carbonyl to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). Then sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine to give sulfonamide linking two aryl rings. In target, sulfonamide connects an aniline (para-methyl phenyl) to a phenyl sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1 (reverse of amide formation): break amide between carbonyl and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursors: carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (aniline with NH2). The amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait SMILES: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So amide formation: carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) + 2-aminophenyl amine? Actually the amine is an aniline with an NH2 (para? not). The amine is an aniline (c3ccccc3N) which has an NH2 group (primary amine). So step: unsaturated acid + 2-aminophenyl amine -> amide.

Step 2: break the unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonate). The unsaturated acid is derived from aromatic aldehyde (likely p-tolyl aldehyde? Actually the aromatic aldehyde is the phenyl ring that later becomes the sulfonyl phenyl? Wait unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? The unsaturated chain is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The unsaturated acid is attached to that phenyl via the double bond? Actually SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has a substituent /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring bearing an aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So step 2: phenyl aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the phenyl ring with methyl) to give sulfonamide linking to the phenyl sulfonyl group. Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... where the N is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So precursors: p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (maybe 4-sulfonyl chloride). But typical sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So we can take p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) and 4-(... )-sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl with the unsaturated side chain). So the sulfonyl chloride is the phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated side chain and a Cl as leaving group on S. So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the phenyl sulfonyl precursor? But we can treat as a step: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide.

Thus retrosynthetic tree:

Target (mol)
- Reaction 1 (retro amide formation): precursors A (α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl) and B (2-aminophenyl, i.e., aniline with NH2). Actually B is 2-aminophenyl? The amide nitrogen attaches to phenyl with NH2 at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an NH2 at position 1 (attached to N) and another NH2? Wait "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates N attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and also an N at the end? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the N attached to carbon is the amide N, and there is an NH2 substituent at the other end of the ring (the terminal N). So the phenyl has an NH2 substituent (aniline). So B is 4-aminophenylamine? Actually it's an aniline with an extra NH2? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That is an aniline where the amide N is attached to carbon 1, and there is an NH2 at the opposite position (maybe para). So B is 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide formation uses p-phenylenediamine (one amine forms amide, the other remains free). So B is p-phenylenediamine.

- Reaction 2 (retro Doebner): precursor A (α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl) -> phenyl aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So we need phenyl aldehyde with the sulfonyl group? Wait the phenyl aldehyde is the same phenyl that later becomes sulfonyl phenyl. So the aldehyde is 4-(sulfonyl phenyl)?? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl via S(=O)2 attached to N of p-tolyl. The phenyl bearing the unsaturated side chain also bears the sulfonyl group attached to N of p-tolyl. So the aldehyde precursor is the same phenyl bearing sulfonyl group (attached to N). So we need sulfonyl chloride? But the sulfonyl group is already present before sulfonamide formation? In forward synthesis, sulfonamide formation is last step, after unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Wait forward order: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (makes amide). 2) Doebner modification (makes unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (makes sulfonamide). So the sulfonamide formation is last, meaning the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl is present before sulfonamide formation. So the phenyl that bears the unsaturated side chain is initially a phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually to form sulfonamide, you need sulfonyl chloride reacting with amine (p-toluidine). So the phenyl sulfonyl chloride must have the unsaturated side chain attached already (i.e., the phenyl ring with the unsaturated side chain and a sulfonyl chloride group). So step 2 yields that phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait step 2 is Doebner modification on aromatic aldehyde to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. That phenyl is the same phenyl that later becomes sulfonyl chloride (by converting the acid to sulfonyl chloride? No, sulfonyl chloride is SCl2 attached to phenyl, not related to acid). Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S(=O)2 attached to N of p-tolyl. The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) as a substituent: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring (c2) via S attached to N of p-tolyl. So the phenyl ring c2 is the sulfonyl phenyl. The unsaturated side chain is attached to that phenyl ring as a substituent. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl ring with a sulfonyl chloride group (SO2Cl) attached to N? Actually sulfonyl chloride is ArSO2Cl. So the phenyl ring c2 would have SO2Cl group (instead of attached to N). Then reacting with p-toluidine (aniline) gives sulfonamide linking them. So step 2 must produce the phenyl sulfonyl chloride with the unsaturated side chain attached. But Doebner modification creates the unsaturated side chain attached to phenyl, not the sulfonyl chloride. The sulfonyl chloride is a separate functional group on the phenyl ring (SO2Cl). So we need to have that functional group present before sulfonamide formation. So the phenyl ring must have both a sulfonyl chloride substituent and the unsaturated side chain. That could be derived from a phenyl sulfonyl chloride that already has the unsaturated side chain attached (i.e., from aldehyde that already has sulfonyl chloride). So the aldehyde precursor for Doebner must be a phenyl aldehyde bearing a sulfonyl chloride group (Ar-CHO where Ar also has SO2Cl). Then Doebner gives unsaturated acid attached to that phenyl with SO2Cl still present. Then sulfonamide formation replaces Cl with N-p-tolyl.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Target -> (retro sulfonamide) gives phenyl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid + p-toluidine.

Step 1: break sulfonamide: product -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) + p-toluidine (4-methylaniline). The sulfonyl chloride retains the unsaturated acid side chain.

Step 2: break amide: sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid -> unsaturated acid (carboxylic acid) + p-phenylenediamine? Wait the amide is attached to p-phenylenediamine, not to sulfonyl chloride. Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to the unsaturated acid carbonyl and to the phenyl ring (c3) which also has an NH2. So the amide formation uses p-phenylenediamine (one amine forms amide, the other remains free). So after step 1, we have sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid attached, and p-toluidine separate. The unsaturated acid still attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. The amide is still present? Wait the amide is part of the unsaturated acid side chain: the unsaturated acid is attached to N of p-phenylenediamine via amide. So after step 1, we still have the amide present. So step 2 (retro amide) splits unsaturated acid (carboxylic acid) from p-phenylenediamine (the amine). So we get unsaturated acid (carboxylic acid) attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride, and p-phenylenediamine.

Step 3 (retro Doebner) splits unsaturated acid into aldehyde (aryl aldehyde bearing sulfonyl chloride) and malonic acid.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine, p-phenylenediamine, malonic acid, and aryl aldehyde bearing sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(chlorosulfonyl)benzaldehyde). That seems plausible.

Now we need to find templates for each step.

We have template for sulfonamide formation (functional groups formed: sulfonamides). The search earlier gave template id 733 (retro smarts: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]). That's a forward reaction: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. Retro direction: break sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and amine. Good.

We need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for amide broken gave template 1664101 but that seems complex. Maybe there is a simpler amide formation template. Let's search for amide formation with functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic acid"]? earlier error due to naming. Use "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's get available functional groups list.
